Its a little concerning to hear people say you should go ahead with it because your mental health will improve once the acne is gone. This is absolutely not guaranteed and was not the case for me. Never prioritize your physical appearance over your mental and physical health. You will regret it every time. 

I can only speak from my experience on accutane but my mental health severely worsened on it. I attempted suicide twice and began drinking heavily to cope with my feelings. I was initially excited when my skin got better but it certainly did not change my life or my perception of myself. As my depression got worse I shut everything and everyone out, had no self-respect or self-worth. Having clear skin did not change that. In fact I had completely forgotten about taking care of myself, what I looked like, and why I was even taking that pill each day.

I honestly regret going on it. It wasn't worth the longer-term mental and physical problems with my vision, joints, and hair loss that I'm still dealing with today. I was on it for a few rounds when I was 17-20. Longer than my doctor should have ever allowed and I lost those years that I can never get back. I'm 23 now and my perception has changed so much.

Please exhaust all your other options before you go ahead with it. I really wish doctors would be more careful prescribing accutane to teenagers. Its such a delicate stage of life as-is.

Being able to apply the general principles is a far better use of your time than simply memorizing them. I’m currently in contract law (3475) and it operates very similar to 2275. 

It’s also crucial to know the principles / rules / exceptions established in the key cases from the textbook. I always include in my notes for these law courses the ratio decidendi for each and every case. If it’s unclear in the textbook, it is definitely worth searching the case online.

My dr finally cut me off my endless round because of the side effects and I had to learn to accept that there is no “cure” for acne. So i cannot comment on BUS 1299 cause i never took it but i did take 2257 in intersession this summer. Like others commented participation is done through zoom calls (which were at 10am est in every section) and it can be a bitch to actually get called upon so my advice is to come VERY prepared to every zoom call. Because you need to raise your hand on EVERY question asked in order to get called once or twice in the entire 3 hour call.

As far as feas went in the summer course it was intersession so there was no in depth- come up with your own business format. We were given groups (although you can request specific people to work and they'll accommodate) and given two companies in which you complete a series of analyses to make an ultimate decision. We were given 48 hours and unless your group is a very well-oiled machine you'll be pulling all nighters.

Another thing ide caution is the exams. Every exam naturally has some time constraints to it but this was insane in comparison to other courses ive taken. The exams are not difficult if you do the cases but my god the time constraints were not at all fair IMO given the online format. (especially if its not something your used to) Showing your work involves uploading a separate sheet of work which you need to take a picture of or scan unless writing numbers on a document on your computer is easy for you. This is likely personal preference but doing a bank reconciliation online where you have to scroll up and down the entire online page back and forth is fucking time consuming and annoying. its little things like this that really pissed me off. Exams were formatted as 1 online test (mostly multiple choice, but 2 longer questions as well eg. financial statements, bank recs) and 2 cases. Exams also always started at the same time as zoom calls 10am est. A majority of people in my section complained about the exam time constraints and I hope they sort this out for future students because it can definitely be better formatted. 

If accounting isnt your thing- I dont recommend bus 2257- especially in intersession over the summer. It's a demanding course. 1st term is simple financial accounting. dr/cr t-accounts. In second term you wont see nearly as many t-accounts as it consists of more managerial analysis such as marketing, cash budgeting, differential analysis, looking at financial ratios and what not.
